title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 5.4 The Lord’s Prayer

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Jesus taught his followers how to pray in Matthew 6:9-13. This prayer is called the Lord's Prayer. In this sub-strand you will recite it, learn what each part means, pray for parents, guardians, friends and relatives, and make prayer a daily habit so that you grow spiritually.

## Strand 5.0: The Church
Sub-strand 5.4: The Lord’s Prayer
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) recite the Lord’s prayer
b) pray for parents, guardians and friends
c) say a prayer to God every day to grow spiritually

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why should you pray always as a Christian?

## Core competencies
• Collaboration: learners develop the skill of teamwork as they discuss, sing and recite the Lord’s Prayer.

## Values
• Unity is enhanced as learners pray for their parents/guardians, friends and relatives.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Developmental perspective: self-discipline is enhanced as learners recite the Lord’s Prayer daily.

## Links to other learning areas
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing.
• English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the Bible.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 5.0 The Church, Sub-strand 5.4 The Lord's Prayer
• Matthew 6:9-13

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Reciting the Lord's Prayer

LESSON 1: RECITING THE LORD'S PRAYER
====================================

## What you will learn
• Read Matthew 6:9-13.
• Recite the Lord's Prayer from memory.

Curriculum outcomes: a) recite the Lord’s prayer

## Introduction
Jesus did not leave his followers without words for prayer. In Matthew 6:9-13 he said, "This is how you should pray," and gave them the prayer Christians still recite.

## Notes
### Where the prayer is found
Read Matthew 6:9-13. Jesus was teaching his disciples. He told them to pray in this way. Christians call it the Lord's Prayer because the Lord Jesus taught it.

Learn to recite it. The words below follow Matthew 6:9-13. Many churches end with the words of praise that the King James Bible includes in verse 13.

Our Father in heaven,
hallowed be your name.
Your kingdom come.
Your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.
Give us today our daily bread.
And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.
For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

### How to learn it
- Read one sentence.
- Say it with the teacher.
- Cover the page and say it again.
- Add the next sentence only when the first one is firm.
- Recite it with a partner, then alone.

Say the words clearly. Do not rush the middle lines about forgiveness and temptation, because those lines are easy to skip. "Amen" means "so be it". It is the way we end the prayer, agreeing with what we have asked.

### Recite it daily
The design asks learners to recite the Lord's Prayer daily. Morning, before lessons, or evening is a good time. Reciting is not a race. It is speaking to God the prayer Jesus gave. In the next lesson you will look at what each line is asking. For this lesson, the aim is to know the words and to say them correctly.

A song that uses the Lord's Prayer can help the memory. Sing it, then speak it without the tune, so that you can recite it even when there is no music.

## Key words
• Lord's Prayer — the prayer Jesus taught his followers in Matthew 6:9-13
• hallowed — honoured as holy
• Amen — so be it; the word that ends the prayer

## Activity: Read and recite Matthew 6:9-13
You will need: Bible, Flash cards with each line of the prayer
1. Sing a song related to the Lord's Prayer.
2. Read Matthew 6:9-13 together.
3. Arrange flash cards of the lines in the correct order.
4. Recite the Lord's Prayer in pairs, then as a class, until you can say it without the cards.

## Practice
1. In which passage did Jesus teach the Lord's Prayer?
2. Recite the Lord's Prayer.
3. What does "Amen" mean at the end of the prayer?
4. Why is this prayer called the Lord's Prayer?

## Summary
• Jesus taught the Lord's Prayer in Matthew 6:9-13.
• It begins "Our Father in heaven" and ends with praise and Amen.
• Christians recite it daily, carefully and from memory.

### Answers to practice
1. Matthew 6:9-13.
2. Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
3. So be it. We agree with the prayer we have prayed.
4. Because the Lord Jesus taught it to his followers.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: What the prayer asks

LESSON 2: WHAT THE PRAYER ASKS
==============================

## What you will learn
• Explain the meaning of each part of the Lord's Prayer.
• Give reasons for praying to God every day.

Curriculum outcomes: a) recite the Lord’s prayer; c) say a prayer to God every day to grow spiritually

## Introduction
Saying the words is the first step. Understanding them keeps the prayer from becoming empty sound. Each line of Matthew 6:9-13 asks God for something, or honours him.

## Notes
### The meaning of the lines
- "Our Father in heaven": We pray to God as Father. "Our" means we pray with other people, not only for ourselves. He is in heaven, above us and holy.
- "Hallowed be your name": We ask that God's name be honoured as holy in our words and in our lives.
- "Your kingdom come": We ask God to reign. We want his rule in our hearts and in the world.
- "Your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven": We ask to do what God wants, here, in the same way heaven does his will.
- "Give us today our daily bread": We ask for what we need this day, beginning with food. We depend on God for daily needs.
- "Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors": Debts here mean our sins. We ask God to forgive us, and we forgive people who have wronged us. The two belong together in the prayer Jesus taught.
- "Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil": We ask God to keep us from falling into sin and to rescue us from the evil one.
- "For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever": We end by praising God. The kingdom, power and glory are his. Amen.

### Why pray every day
Prayer is talking with God. Jesus taught his followers to pray, so prayer is part of Christian life, not an extra for Sundays only.

- We thank God.
- We ask for daily needs.
- We ask for forgiveness and for strength against temptation.
- We grow spiritually. A person who speaks with God every day stays close to him and learns to want what God wants.

You can pray in the morning, at meals, in the evening, and whenever you are afraid or thankful. Reciting the Lord's Prayer can be one of those times. Other simple prayers, in your own words, belong in the day as well.

Discuss this with the class: a day with no prayer is a day in which we forget to speak to our Father. A short prayer is better than none.

## Key words
• will of God — what God wants to be done
• debts — in this prayer, the sins for which we need forgiveness
• temptation — a pull towards sin; we ask God not to let us fall into it
• grow spiritually — to become closer to God and stronger in faith

## Activity: Match each line to its meaning
You will need: Bible, Strips of paper
1. Read Matthew 6:9-13 again.
2. In groups, discuss why it is important to pray every day.
3. Write each line of the Lord's Prayer on a strip and, beside it, the meaning in your own words.
4. Recite the prayer daily. List how many times you prayed yesterday and be ready to share the number with classmates in the next lesson.

## Practice
1. What are we asking when we say "Hallowed be your name"?
2. What does "Give us today our daily bread" ask for?
3. What do "debts" mean in the Lord's Prayer, and what must we also do?
4. Give two reasons why a Christian should pray every day.

## Summary
• Each line of the Lord's Prayer honours God or asks for his help.
• We ask for daily needs, forgiveness, and deliverance from evil.
• Praying every day helps a Christian grow spiritually.

### Answers to practice
1. That God's name will be honoured as holy.
2. Our needs for the day, beginning with food.
3. Our sins. We ask God to forgive us, and we forgive our debtors, the people who have wronged us.
4. Any two: Jesus taught us to pray; we thank God and ask for our needs; we ask for forgiveness and help against temptation; we grow spiritually by staying close to God.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Praying for others every day

LESSON 3: PRAYING FOR OTHERS EVERY DAY
======================================

## What you will learn
• Pray for parents, guardians, friends and relatives.
• Plan a daily time of prayer.

Curriculum outcomes: b) pray for parents, guardians and friends; c) say a prayer to God every day to grow spiritually

## Introduction
The Lord's Prayer says "our" and "us", not only "my" and "me". Jesus taught us to pray with other people in mind. Christians pray for parents, guardians, friends and relatives, and they do it every day.

## Notes
### Who we pray for
Unity grows when we bring other people to God instead of thinking only of ourselves.

- Parents and guardians: thank God for them. Ask him to give them health, work, wisdom and peace. Ask him to help you honour them.
- Friends: ask God to help them at school, to keep them safe, and to help you be a kind and truthful friend.
- Relatives: brothers, sisters, grandparents and other family members. Pray for those who are sick, those who are away, and those who do not yet know God.

You do not need long words. "Lord, bless my mother and keep her safe today" is a real prayer. You may also use the Lord's Prayer and then add these names.

### A daily prayer
Choose a time you can keep: after waking, before you sleep, or both. In that time:

1. Recite the Lord's Prayer.
2. Thank God for one thing.
3. Pray for a parent or guardian, a friend and a relative by name.
4. Ask God to keep you from sin today.
5. End with Amen.

Count the times you pray in a day and share the number with classmates. The number is not a competition. It helps you see whether prayer is really happening. If you prayed only once, you can add an evening prayer. If you forgot, begin again the next morning. Self-discipline grows when the recital is daily, not only when the teacher is listening.

### Growing spiritually
Spiritual growth is a closer walk with God. Daily prayer is one way it happens. You remember that God is Father, that you need forgiveness, and that other people need his help too. A class that prays for one another is a class that is learning the "our" of the Lord's Prayer.

## Key words
• guardian — a person who cares for a child in the place of a parent
• relative — a member of your family
• daily prayer — speaking to God every day, not only sometimes

## Activity: Pray for people we love
You will need: Exercise book
1. Recite the Lord's Prayer together.
2. Pray for your parents or guardians, your friends and your relatives. You may pray aloud or quietly.
3. List the number of times you prayed yesterday or today and share the number with a classmate.
4. Write a simple daily plan: the time you will pray, and three people you will name.

## Practice
1. Name three groups of people Christians should pray for in this lesson.
2. Give one thing you can ask God for on behalf of your parents or guardians.
3. What can you include in a daily prayer time?
4. Why does daily prayer help you grow spiritually?

## Summary
• Pray for parents, guardians, friends and relatives by name.
• Recite the Lord's Prayer every day and add your own thanks and requests.
• Daily prayer helps Christians grow spiritually and live in unity.

### Answers to practice
1. Parents or guardians, friends, and relatives.
2. Any one real need, for example health, work, wisdom, peace, or help as they care for the family.
3. The Lord's Prayer, thanks, prayer for a parent or guardian, a friend and a relative, a prayer for help against sin, and Amen.
4. It keeps you close to God, reminds you to depend on him, and teaches you to care for other people before him.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 5.4 THE LORD’S PRAYER
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Where is the Lord's Prayer written?
   A. Matthew 6:9-13
   B. Acts 7:54-60
   C. Genesis 39:7-12
   D. Matthew 10:1-4

2. The Lord's Prayer begins with:
   A. Our Father in heaven
   B. Lord Jesus, receive my spirit
   C. Let the little children come
   D. Repent and be baptized

3. "Hallowed be your name" means:
   A. Give us money
   B. May your name be honoured as holy
   C. Do not forgive us
   D. Lead us into temptation

4. In the Lord's Prayer, "debts" means:
   A. School fees only
   B. Our sins
   C. The tables of the money changers
   D. Daily bread

5. Recite the two lines that ask God to forgive us and to keep us from evil.

6. Why should a Christian pray every day?
   A. So that other people will praise them
   B. To talk with God, receive help, and grow spiritually
   C. Only to pass a test
   D. Because prayer replaces obedience

7. Which people should you pray for?
   A. Only yourself
   B. Parents or guardians, friends and relatives
   C. Only strangers you will never meet
   D. Nobody; the Lord's Prayer forbids names

8. Give one prayer you can say for a friend.

9. What does a daily prayer time help you to do?
   A. Grow spiritually
   B. Avoid all work
   C. Skip church
   D. Forget other people

10. Why does the prayer say "our" Father and "our" daily bread?
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 5.4 THE LORD’S PRAYER
========================================

1. A. Matthew 6:9-13
   Jesus taught this prayer in Matthew 6:9-13.

2. A. Our Father in heaven
   Matthew 6:9 starts the prayer with Our Father in heaven.

3. B. May your name be honoured as holy
   Hallowed means honoured as holy.

4. B. Our sins
   We ask God to forgive our sins, as we forgive those who wrong us.

5. Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.
   These lines are part of Matthew 6:12-13.

6. B. To talk with God, receive help, and grow spiritually
   Daily prayer keeps a believer close to God.

7. B. Parents or guardians, friends and relatives
   The lesson guides learners to pray for parents, guardians, friends and relatives.

8. Any suitable request, for example: Lord, help my friend to learn well and to be safe.
   Praying for friends is part of caring for them before God.

9. A. Grow spiritually
   Saying a prayer to God every day helps a Christian grow spiritually.

10. We pray together and we include other people, not only ourselves.
   The plural words teach unity and care for others.
